# UniProt Keyword Enrichment



This page documents `notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb`, the fifth stage of the mdSAM analysis pipeline. The notebook asks a specific functional-genomics question: which **UniProt keywords** are statistically over- or under-represented among proteins discovered by mdSAM, relative to the broader population of annotated human entries? It answers this with a hypergeometric over-representation test over a two-by-two contingency built from an id-mapping export, then layers a series of publication-grade visualizations (donut, rank, volcano, stacked bar, radar, Sankey, clustermap) and a final embedding analysis that projects binary keyword profiles into 2D space via UMAP and PCA. Unlike the pipeline's engineerd modules, this notebook is a **curated exploratory artifact**: the committed version contains dead demo cells, toggled filters, and local file paths — all of which are documented here so you can reproduce or adapt it deliberately rather than archaeologically.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L32-L39), [files/README.md](files/README.md#L7-L9)

## Position in the Analysis Pipeline

Within the *Sequence Space Characterization* block, notebook 05 is the **functional annotation lens** applied to mdSAM hits after their sequence-level properties have been characterized (composition in notebook 03, physicochemical clustering in notebook 06, PASTA comparison in notebook 04). It consumes the two shared pickle tables documented in [Shared Data Tables Reference](8-shared-data-tables-reference) — the mdSAM discovery table and the AlphaFold annotation table — and joins them against two externally downloaded UniProt exports. Its outputs feed the interpretive narrative that continues in [hyperLOPIT Organelle Enrichment](14-hyperlopit-organelle-enrichment), which repeats the same enrichment pattern against a different annotation system. The complete internal data flow is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph inputs["Data inputs"]
        M["dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl<br/>(mdSAM accessions: acc)"]
        A["AF2_with_ENSG.pkl<br/>(acc, pLDDT bands)"]
        K["keywords_all_2023_10_27.tsv<br/>(Keyword ID, Name, Category)"]
        U["idmapping_2023_10_27.tsv<br/>(Entry, Keyword ID)"]
    end
    K --> IDs["IDs set: BP + MF keyword IDs"]
    U --> KEY["KEYdf long table (ID, description, acc)"]
    IDs --> KEY
    KEY --> CNT["KEYdf_counts: keyword frequencies"]
    CNT --> TOP["top_IDs frequency window 1-1500"]
    TOP --> CT["top_IDs_df / top_IDs_total<br/>+/- contingency (percent, counts)"]
    M --> CT
    CT --> HG["hypergeom() + BH FDR -> df_volcano"]
    HG --> XLS["UniProt_Keyword_enrich.xlsx"]
    HG --> FIG["Volcano, rank, donut, bar,<br/>radar, Sankey, clustermap figures"]
    U --> BM["Binary acc-by-keyword matrix<br/>(pLDDT != A filter)"]
    A --> BM
    M --> BM
    BM --> EMB["UMAP + PCA embeddings"]
    EMB --> SM["Per-keyword small multiples"]
```

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L32-L39), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2136-L2148), [files/README.md](files/README.md#L7-L9)

## Data Inputs and the Annotation Universe

The notebook loads four tables in its second cell. Two come from the shared `../files/` directory: the **mdSAM table** (whose `.acc` column supplies the discovery set) and the **AlphaFold table** (whose `.acc` and `.pLDDT` columns are used later for embedding-space filtering). Two are *local* TSV exports with dated filenames — `keywords_all_2023_10_27.tsv` (the UniProt keyword taxonomy: `Keyword ID`, `Name`, `Category`) and `idmapping_2023_10_27.tsv` (per-entry keyword assignments in an `Entry` / `Keyword ID` layout) — loaded from the original author's Downloads folder. Note that `files/README.md` lists `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` as the shared resource "read by notebook 05"; the committed notebook instead reads the id-mapping TSV directly, so when adapting the notebook you should either regenerate that export or point the read at the shared pickle.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L32-L39), [files/README.md](files/README.md#L7-L9)

The id-mapping table, renamed `hTMs_uniprot`, plays a dual role that defines the notebook's statistics. It is first filtered to entries whose `Keywords` field is non-null (line 37), and this filtered frame then serves as the **annotation universe** — the population *N* against which all enrichment is measured. Every contingency, expectation, and p-value in the notebook is therefore conditioned on "annotated entries", not on the complete proteome. A commented-out fragment inside the keyword-extraction loop (`hTMs_uniprot.Entry.isin(mdSAM.acc)`) reveals that the extraction once ran on the mdSAM subset only and was widened to the full universe, so membership is now applied *later*, at the contingency stage rather than the extraction stage. Keep this scope in mind when comparing p-values against tools like DAVID or g:Profiler, which use different background definitions.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L36-L37), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L80-L86)

## Building the Keyword Contingency Table

The transformation chain proceeds in four stages. First, a **category scope filter** selects keyword IDs from `KeyWord_df` whose `Category` is `Biological process` or `Molecular function` into the `IDs` set; a trailing comment shows `Disease` was toggled in and out during the session, and downstream cells (hand-picked keywords including `Epilepsy`, a Disease keyword; volcano plots with a Disease hue entry) confirm the final runs included it. Second, the notebook explodes the semicolon-separated `Keyword ID` field: for every annotated entry it intersects the entry's keyword set with `IDs` and emits one record per keyword into the long-format `KEYdf` (`ID`, `disrcption`, `acc`). Third, `KEYdf_counts` aggregates this into per-keyword frequencies. Fourth, a **frequency window** — `counts_total.between(1, 1500)` — produces `top_IDs`, excluding both ubiquitous keywords (which would dominate any ratio) and singletons (which carry no statistical weight).

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L48-L58), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L80-L95), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L178), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L494-L510)

The core cell then sweeps `top_IDs` and builds the contingency semantics that drive everything downstream. For each keyword it counts entries whose `Keyword ID` string contains the keyword ID, split by membership in `mdSAM.acc`, and pivots the results two ways: `top_IDs_df` holds **percentages** of the keyword's carriers inside vs. outside mdSAM, while `top_IDs_total` holds raw **counts** in `+` and `-` columns. A keyword-level `Category` column (mapped back from the full keyword taxonomy) and a hand-picked highlight list (`Cell adhesion`, `G-protein coupled receptor`, `Differentiation`, `Immunity`, `Ion transport`, `Kinase`, `Epilepsy`) decorate these tables for plotting. Conceptually:

```mermaid
graph LR
    UNI["Annotation universe hTMs_uniprot"] -->|"Entry in mdSAM.acc"| IN["Quadrant +: carriers in mdSAM"]
    UNI -->|"complement"| OUT["Quadrant -: carriers outside mdSAM"]
    KW["Keyword KW-XXXX<br/>substring match in Keyword ID field"] --> W["Winners: all carriers"]
    W --> IN
    W --> OUT
    IN --> OBS["observed k"]
    W --> EXP["expected A x W / N"]
    OBS --> TAIL["Hypergeometric tail test"]
    EXP --> TAIL
    TAIL --> BH["Benjamini-Hochberg FDR"]
```

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L198-L218), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L293-L306), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L349-L352)

## The Hypergeometric Over-Representation Test

The `hypergeom()` function is the notebook's statistical engine, phrased in a memorable "team A / winners" metaphor. Given a keyword name, it assembles the four quantities of a hypergeometric experiment from the contingency tables and calls `stats.hypergeom.cdf`. The expected count is the classic ratio `A·W/N`:

| Code variable | Statistical role | Computed as |
|---|---|---|
| `total_runners` | Population size *N* | `len(hTMs_uniprot)` — all annotated entries |
| `number_team_A` | Draw size *A* (mdSAM hits) | entries with `Entry.isin(mdSAM.acc)` |
| `number_winners` | Successes in population *W* | `+` + `-` counts for the keyword |
| `number_win_from_A` | Observed successes *k* | `+` count for the keyword |
| `expected` | Mean of the null | `A·W/N` |
| `p` | Tail probability | `stats.hypergeom.cdf(k, N, W, A)`, flipped when over-represented |

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L590-L601)

> [!TIP]
> Watch the tail semantics: `stats.hypergeom.cdf(k, N, W, A)` returns the *lower* tail P(X ≤ k). When `k > expected` the function flips it to `1 − p`, which equals P(X ≥ k+1) — so the reported over-representation p-values are **conservative by exactly one observation** relative to the canonical P(X ≥ k) of a Fisher exact test. This matters if you cross-check the notebook's numbers against `scipy.stats.hypergeom.sf` or `fisher_exact`.

The driver loop applies `hypergeom()` across `df_total`, collecting observed, expected, and p-values into `df_volcano`, then computes **Benjamini–Hochberg FDR** inline: p-values are ranked with `rankdata`, scaled by `p·n/rank`, capped at 1, and expressed as `fdr_log = −log10(fdr)`. The complete result table is exported to `UniProt_Keyword_enrich.xlsx`, making this cell the notebook's durable analytical output. Note that a standalone `fdr()` helper defined earlier computes the identical correction but omits a `return` statement — the inline block is the operative implementation.

> [!TIP]
> When adapting the FDR logic, reuse the inline block at lines 656–661 rather than the `fdr()` helper at lines 611–615: the helper's missing `return` silently yields `None`. Also note the driver drops rows with `pval == 0` before correction — underflowed exact-zero p-values from huge keywords are excluded from the FDR family rather than floored.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L636-L644), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L656-L671), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L611-L615)

## Figure Inventory and Design Patterns

The plotting layer converts `df_volcano` and the contingency tables into the paper's figure set. Two design conventions recur throughout: a **fixed category color system** (Biological process `#13609A`/`#125F99`, Molecular function `#3D3E3C`, Disease `#766094`/`#6E578E`, mdSAM-positive red `#C03830` vs. gray `#B4B5B4`) and **`adjust_text` label repulsion** applied to significant keywords only. The notebook also registers a custom `radar_factory` matplotlib projection twice — once early, once mid-notebook with a slightly different `PolarTransform` override — so the second definition wins at runtime; both exist to draw the polygon-frame radar charts used as "spider" summaries.

| Output file | Chart type | Encodes |
|---|---|---|
| `donut_v4.svg` | Donut with count annotations | Top keywords by `+` count, category-colored, hand-picked slices exploded |
| `volcano_<Category>.svg` | Rank plot (per category) | Keywords sorted by `obs_exp`; point size = `−log10 FDR`; FDR-log > 2 colored, others gray |
| `c.svg` | Broken-axis volcano | `obs_exp` vs. `fdr_log` with dashed gates at ±11 and 3 |
| `Biological_top_Keyword_bar.svg` | Stacked fraction bar | `+_ratio` vs. `-_ratio` per keyword from the `zz` ratio table, plus a `Base ratio` reference bar |
| `<Category>_top_Keyword_spider.svg` | Radar | Per-category `+_ratio` (red) vs. `-_ratio` (gray) against the dashed base-ratio circle |
| `mdSAM_all_left2right.svg` | Sankey (holoviews/bokeh) | Keyword → `+` flows for the 11 strongest and 5 weakest keywords |
| *(inline)* clustermaps/heatmaps | `sns.clustermap` / `sns.heatmap` | Receptor and Transport contingency percentages annotated with raw counts |

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L527-L547), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L766-L794), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L834-L901), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1350-L1386), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1557-L1574), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1714-L1736), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2025-L2047)

Two implementation details deserve maintainer awareness. The stacked bars and radar charts read from a `zz` table (columns `word`, `cat`, `+`, `-`, `+_ratio`, `-_ratio`) together with a scalar `ratio_base`; only their *consumption* is in the visible cells, so if you rebuild the notebook from scratch you must reconstruct that aggregation from `top_IDs_total`. And the Sankey/chord section imports holoviews with bokeh sample airport data — those are verbatim demo cells from the holoviews gallery left in place; only the final `hv.Sankey(l)` calls operate on real data.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1350-L1359), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1523-L1529), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1600-L1621)

## Conditional Sub-Analyses: Co-occurrence Gating

Beyond the global test, the notebook demonstrates a reusable pattern: **enrichment within an annotation-conditioned subset**. The `SuperKeys(ID)` function counts which other keywords co-occur with a seed keyword across all entries carrying that seed, producing a co-annotation frequency profile for any `KW-XXXX`. The Transport analysis operationalizes the same idea with a *double* string filter — an entry must contain both the transport-family keyword *and* a fixed gate keyword `KW-0813` — before splitting by mdSAM membership, yielding `Transport_df` (percent) and `Transport_df_values` (counts) that feed a cosine-metric clustermap and sorted heatmap. A parallel `Receptor_df` block does the same for receptor-family keywords. This gating answers a sharper question than the global test: *among transporters, which transport modalities characterize mdSAM hits?*

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L154-L168), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1982-L2005), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2025-L2047)

The section also contains two numerical hygiene steps worth copying into any adaptation. A **pseudocount** (`top_IDs_total.loc['Electron transport']['+'] = 1`) prevents a zero cell from breaking downstream ratios and chi-square computation, and a **chi-square normalization** divides the contingency table by `stats.chi2_contingency(...)` output to produce the weighted table `w` used for one of the ranking views. These are ad hoc stabilizers rather than part of the primary hypergeometric result, but they illustrate how the notebook guards degenerate cells in sparse annotation data.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1633), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L1643-L1644)

## Keyword Profiles as High-Dimensional Vectors

The final third of the notebook reframes enrichment geometrically. A nested loop builds a **binary acc-by-keyword matrix** `x`: every entry annotated with at least one keyword from the 10–2000 frequency window is crossed with every keyword in that window, marked 1/0 by substring match, and pivoted wide. The matrix is then filtered to entries whose AlphaFold table row has `pLDDT != 'A'` — excluding proteins whose AFDB banded confidence falls in the lowest band — tying annotation structure to model confidence. This is the notebook's bridge to the *sequence space* narrative: proteins become points whose coordinates are their functional annotation fingerprint, and the question becomes whether mdSAM hits occupy annotation space coherently rather than merely testing keyword frequencies.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2103-L2126)

Two embeddings are computed on `x`: **UMAP** (`random_state=42, n_neighbors=10`) colored by mdSAM membership, and **PCA** (`n_components=2`) with the same coloring at low alpha; a second UMAP variant explores the sparse binary space with `n_neighbors=2, metric='manhattan'`. TSNE is imported but its invocation is commented out — UMAP and PCA are the live paths. Both embeddings are then decomposed into an **11×10 grid of per-keyword small multiples**: each panel highlights the entries carrying one keyword on the shared embedding, letting you read which annotation neighborhoods mdSAM points fall into. A follow-up loop re-annotates the PCA frame with human-readable keyword-name columns via per-entry substring matching against the universe table.

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2136-L2148), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2158-L2186), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2229-L2280), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2330-L2342), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2201-L2209)

## Reproducing and Adapting the Notebook

The notebook is executable from `notebooks/` as the working directory (the shared pickles are addressed as `../files/...`). Before running, you must supply the two UniProt exports — both are dated 2023-10-27 snapshots, so re-download current keyword and id-mapping files from UniProt and update the local paths in the loading cell, or regenerate `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` per [Shared Data Tables Reference](8-shared-data-tables-reference). Non-stdlib dependencies beyond the pipeline norm include `umap-learn`, `adjustText`, `cmasher`, and `holoviews`/`bokeh` (only needed for the Sankey section). As with all shared pickles in this repository, `pd.read_pickle` executes stored code — load them only from this repo with a compatible pandas version.

| Knob | Location | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Category scope (`IDs`) | Category filter cell | BP + MF, Disease toggleable | Which keyword families enter `KEYdf` |
| Frequency window (contingency) | `top_IDs` | 1–1500 | Drops ubiquitous keywords and singletons |
| Frequency window (binary matrix) | `accs`/`keys` | 10–2000 | Density threshold for the embedding input |
| FDR display threshold | rank/volcano plots | `fdr_log > 2` (FDR < 0.01) | Which keywords are colored/labeled |
| Volcano label gates | volcano cells | `fdr_log ∈ (3, 35)`, `\|obs_exp\| > 11` | Which points receive text labels |
| UMAP parameters | embedding cells | seed 42; n_neighbors 10 (variant: 2, manhattan) | Geometry of annotation space |
| Co-occurrence gate | Transport block | fixed `KW-0813` seed | Subset within which transport keywords are compared |

Sources: [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L32-L39), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L178), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2103-L2104), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L2136-L2136), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L775-L779), [notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb](notebooks/05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb#L808-L808), [files/README.md](files/README.md#L3-L13)

## Where to Go Next

To understand where the mdSAM accessions feeding this enrichment come from, start with [mdSAM Concept and Discovery Rationale](4-mdsam-concept-and-discovery-rationale) and [WALTZ-DB Random-Forest Classifier](6-waltz-db-random-forest-classifier); the `pLDDT` filtering used in the embedding section is contextualized in [AlphaFold-Based Disorder Filtering](7-alphafold-based-disorder-filtering). # hyperLOPIT Organelle Enrichment



This page explains `07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb`, the notebook that tests whether mdSAM-bearing membrane proteins are systematically enriched in specific subcellular compartments. The strategy is not a database lookup: the notebook re-quantifies a published hyperLOPIT fractionation dataset (Thul et al., U2OS cells), clusters transmembrane proteins by their 10-channel TMT fractionation profile, labels each cluster with a compartment identity, and then runs a Fisher exact test asking whether mdSAM proteins are over-represented in each compartment relative to expectation. Along the way it produces the replicate-quality-control figures, the t-SNE compartment map, and the observed-vs-expected bar chart that back the paper's localization claims.

The notebook sits between sequence-space characterization and the topology analysis: [UniProt Keyword Enrichment](13-uniprot-keyword-enrichment) asked *what functions* mdSAM proteins share, this page asks *where they live*, and [Topology and Membrane-Leaflet Distance](15-topology-and-membrane-leaflet-distance) follows with *which side of the membrane they face*.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L270-L286), [files/README.md](/files/README.md#L5-L11)

## Analysis Pipeline at a Glance

The notebook is best understood as five sequential stages, each physically separated by markdown-free code cells in the file. Data flows from a wide Excel quantitation table into a tidy long-format frame, gets clustered in an unsupervised embedding, and terminates in a contingency-table test. Note the two asymmetric data paths: the `hyperLOPIT` frame (built from raw Excel) is used for QC and clustering, while `frac_plot_df` (loaded from a local pickle and rebuilt mid-notebook) carries the per-accession annotations used for plotting.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Thul et al. S12 Excel<br/>(hyperLOPIT Quantitation Data)"] -->|melt 10 TMT channels<br/>x 2 replicates| B["hyperLOPIT long table<br/>acc / fraction / val / Replicate"]
    B -->|"flag tm (hTMs)<br/>flag mdSAM (dSAM.acc)"| C["QC: Rep1 vs Rep2<br/>Pearson r per channel"]
    B --> D["Pivot: TM proteins<br/>x 10 channels"]
    D -->|t-SNE perplexity=10| E["2D embedding"]
    E -->|GMM n=8, tied cov| F["8 raw clusters"]
    F -->|remap dict d| G["gmm_new 0-4:<br/>PM / ER / Endo-Lyso / Golgi / Other"]
    G -->|"2x2 table per cluster<br/>(741 neg, 159 pos)"| H["Fisher exact +<br/>log2(obs/exp)"]
    H --> I["Observed vs Expected<br/>bar chart per compartment"]
    G --> J["Compartment fidelity heatmap<br/>markers x GMM cluster"]
```

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L328-L347), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L840-L871), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1284-L1311)

## Data Inputs and Provenance

Four external sources converge in this notebook, and their provenance matters for reproducing the analysis. The two Excel files are supplementary tables downloaded from published studies and referenced by **absolute local paths** — they are not shipped with the repository. The three pickles come from the shared `files/` directory and are documented in [Shared Data Tables Reference](8-shared-data-tables-reference); note that `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl` is listed as an input but is not present in the current repository tree, so the IDR-count step depends on regenerating it (see [AlphaFold-Based Disorder Filtering](7-alphafold-based-disorder-filtering)).

| Input | Origin | Loaded at | Role in analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aal3321_thul_sm_table_s12.xlsx`, sheet *hyperLOPIT Quantitation Data* | Thul et al. supplementary table (U2OS hyperLOPIT) | `raw` | Source of TMT per-fraction intensities |
| `elife-16950-supp1-v3.xlsx`, sheet *Organellar Markers HeLa* | eLife-16950 supplementary | `markers` | Compartment ground truth (`Compartment` column) |
| `dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl` | mdSAM identification pipeline | `dSAM` | mdSAM membership via `acc` column |
| `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` | produced by notebook 03 | `hTMs` | Transmembrane universe via `acc` column |
| `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl` | produced by notebook 02 | `AF2` | Per-protein `pLDDT` arrays → disordered-residue count |
| `HPA_frac_df.pkl`, `HPA_anaysis/frac_plot_df.pkl` | prior local runs of this notebook | `xx`, `frac_plot_df` | Pre-annotated plotting tables (`gmm_new`, `mdSAM`, `idr`) |

The marker table is loaded from the *Organellar Markers HeLa* sheet even though the quantitation is U2OS — the marker list serves purely as compartment ground truth for labeling clusters, while the fractionation profiles themselves are U2OS-derived (plot titles read `$U2OS\;hyperLOPIT$`).

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L270-L286), [files/README.md](/files/README.md#L5-L13), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L756-L757)

## From Wide TMT Table to Tidy Fractionation Profiles

The raw hyperLOPIT table stores intensities in a wide layout with TMT channel columns suffixed by replicate. The notebook defines the ten channel stems once — `['126','127C','127N','128C','128N','129C','129N','130C','130N','131']` — and melts the table by iterating over every accession × channel pair, taking the mean of the non-null `Replicate1` and `Replicate2` columns separately. The result is the canonical long frame `hyperLOPIT` with columns `acc`, `fraction`, `val`, `Replicate`.

Two boolean flags are then painted onto every row: `tm` (`yes`/`no`, membership in `hTMs.acc`) and `mdSAM` (`yes`/`no`, membership in `dSAM.acc`). These two columns are the entire definition of the analysis universes — every downstream contingency table is a cross-tabulation of them, so auditing these join keys is the fastest way to audit the results.

> [!TIP]
> The `filter(regex=i)` channel matching is prefix-based: channel stem `126` will also match columns like `126C_Replicate1`, which is exactly the intended behavior here, but it means adding any other column containing `126` (e.g., an unrelated metadata column) would silently contaminate the mean.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L328-L329), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L339-L347), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L358-L367)

## Replicate Quality Control

Before any biology is interpreted, the notebook validates the hyperLOPIT quantitation. TM proteins' intensities are paired as `x` = Replicate 1 vs `y` = Replicate 2 per channel into the frame `c3`, and Pearson correlation coefficients are computed per TMT channel. Three figures come out of this stage: a 5×2 panel of per-channel replicate scatter plots (`hyperLOPIT_TM_corr_v2.svg`), a single combined scatter with a global *r* annotation and identity line (`hyperLOPIT_TM_corr.svg`), and a horizontal bar chart of per-channel *r* values on a fixed 0.65–0.95 axis (`hyperLOPIT_TM_corr_bar.svg`). The fixed axis limits are a deliberate presentation choice — they keep all channels visually comparable rather than letting each bar auto-scale.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L379-L392), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L439-L460), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L497-L507)

## Compartment Clustering: t-SNE + Gaussian Mixture

This is the notebook's central methodological move. Instead of trusting protein-to-compartment assignments for every protein, only the *marker* proteins are trusted, and all other TM proteins are assigned by the shape of their fractionation profile:

1. **Pivot**: TM proteins (`tm == 'yes'`) become a matrix `xx` of accession × 10 channels (mean over replicates).
2. **Embed**: `TSNE(n_components=2, learning_rate='auto', init='random', perplexity=10)` compresses each profile to a 2D point.
3. **Cluster**: `mixture.GaussianMixture(n_components=8, covariance_type="tied")` is fit on the embedding coordinates.
4. **Consolidate**: a hardcoded remap dictionary `d = {2:0, 6:0, 0:1, 5:1, 7:1, 1:2, 3:3, 4:4}` collapses the 8 raw components into the 5 interpretable clusters stored in `gmm_new`.
5. **Name**: the notebook annotates the t-SNE plot with canonical marker proteins per cluster — SSR1/RTN1/STX5/MIA3/SARAF for ER, ADGRB1/APP/NGFR/MET/CDH2 for PM, GOLIN4/MAN1A2/QSOX2/GLG1/MAN1B1 for Golgi, ATG9A/SORT1/ATP13A3 for Endo/Lyso — fixing the label-to-number mapping as PM=0, ER=1, Endo/Lyso=2, Golgi=3, Other=4.

Each accession also receives an `idr` column (count of AF2 residues with pLDDT < 70) and `mdSAM` polarity labels rendered as `+`/`−` for plotting.

| `gmm_new` | Compartment label | Constituent raw GMM components |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Plasma membrane (PM) | 2, 6 |
| 1 | ER | 0, 5, 7 |
| 2 | Endo/Lyso | 1 |
| 3 | Golgi | 3 |
| 4 | Other | 4 |

> [!TIP]
> Neither `TSNE` nor `GaussianMixture` is given a `random_state`, and t-SNE with `init='random'` is stochastic. Re-running this cell will produce a different embedding and different raw component numbering, so the remap dictionary `d` is valid only for the run that produced it — treat `gmm_new` in any cached pickle as the authoritative cluster identity, and re-derive `d` by marker-protein inspection if you recluster.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L840-L871), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L892-L895), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L958-L971)

## Enrichment Statistics: Fisher Exact per Compartment

The headline test is deliberately simple. For each of the five clusters, a 2×2 contingency table contrasts mdSAM-negative versus mdSAM-positive TM proteins inside the cluster against their totals outside it, with the background hardcoded as **741 negative** and **159 positive** TM proteins. `scipy.stats.fisher_exact` yields the two-sided p-value, `scipy.stats.contingency.expected_freq` yields the expected count under independence, and enrichment is quantified as `enrich = np.log2(observed / expected)`.

| Cluster axis | Recorded fields |
|---|---|
| Per-cluster result | `gmm_cluster`, `gmm_cluster_size`, `obs`, `exp`, `pval`, `enrich` |
| Test universe | 741 mdSAM− TMs + 159 mdSAM+ TMs (900 total) |
| Effect size | log2(observed / expected mdSAM count) |

The results are assembled into `fisher_bar` and rendered as an observed-vs-expected grouped bar chart (`hyperLOPIT_enrich_v2.svg`), where the expected bars are hatch-patterned and both bar groups are colored per compartment, with x labels `$PM$`, `$ER$`, `$Endo/Lyso$`, `$Golgi$`, `$Other$`. The `$n=900\,MPs$` annotation used elsewhere in the notebook's profile plots corresponds to the same 741 + 159 universe. This is an enrichment-by-localization complement to the keyword-based enrichment in [UniProt Keyword Enrichment](13-uniprot-keyword-enrichment), which uses the same +/− universe logic but ontology terms instead of compartments.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1284-L1311), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1320-L1322), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1396-L1443)

## Cluster Validation Against Marker Ground Truth

Because the clustering is unsupervised, the notebook includes two validation layers. First, a compartment-purity matrix: for every marker compartment (Plasma membrane, ER, ERGIC, ER_high_curvature, Endosome, Lysosome, Golgi, Mitochondrion, Nuclear pore complex, Peroxisome) and every GMM cluster, it computes the percentage of that compartment's marker proteins falling into the cluster, rendered as the "Organelle fiducial markers" heatmap (`hyperLOPIT_tsne_2_matrix.svg`). Off-diagonal mass here would indicate profile-shape clusters that split or merge true compartments. Second, a per-cluster fractionation profile gallery (`hyperLOPIT_compartments.svg`) overlaying individual protein traces within each cluster, plus a cividis clustermap of the acc × channel matrix (`hyperLOPIT_clustermap.svg`) that shows the dendrogram structure of the profiles directly. A compartment-level mdSAM overlay (`hyperLOPIT_raw.svg`) plots `val_100` (percent-normalized intensity) traces for mdSAM+ (red `#C03830`) versus mdSAM− (gray) proteins, providing the qualitative "mdSAM proteins look like they peak somewhere" evidence that the Fisher test then formalizes.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1132-L1172), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1250-L1257), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L652-L672)

## Supporting Visualization Utilities

The first substantive cell block defines `calculate_hull`, `draw_hull`, and `draw_rounded_hull` — generic convex-hull drawing helpers. `calculate_hull` scales the point cloud, computes a `scipy.spatial.ConvexHull`, and smooths the boundary via periodic spline interpolation (`quadratic_periodic` by default through `scipy.interpolate.splev`); `draw_rounded_hull` instead rounds hull corners by inset lines and `matplotlib.patches.Arc` segments. These are used to draw smooth compartment boundaries around each GMM cluster in the publication t-SNE (`hyperLOPIT_tsne_v5.svg`), which drops axes and labels in favor of hull silhouettes with mdSAM+ points overplotted in red.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L40-L238), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L999-L1033)

## Reproducibility Notes and Pitfalls

Running this notebook end-to-end requires more than the repository contains. The practical blockers, in the order you will hit them:

| Issue | Detail | Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| Absolute download paths | `/Users/aelazar/Downloads/aal3321_thul_sm_table_s12.xlsx` and `elife-16950-supp1-v3.xlsx` | Download both supplementary files and rewrite the two `read_excel` paths |
| Missing intermediate pickles | `HPA_frac_df.pkl` and `HPA_anaysis/frac_plot_df.pkl` are loaded at the top but live outside the repo | Recreate by running the notebook's own pivot/annotation cells; create `HPA_anaysis/` for the SVG outputs |
| Missing shared pickle | `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl` is read but absent from `files/` in the current tree | Regenerate via [AlphaFold-Based Disorder Filtering](7-alphafold-based-disorder-filtering) (notebook 02) |
| Working directory | `../files/...` references assume `notebooks/` as CWD | Follow the convention stated in `files/README.md` |
| Stochastic clustering | t-SNE and GMM run without `random_state` | Seed both, and re-derive the 8→5 remap `d` by checking marker-protein positions per cluster |
| Hardcoded test totals | Fisher table uses fixed `741` / `159` background counts | If your dSAM or hTMs tables differ from the paper versions, compute these totals from `xx.mdSAM.value_counts()` before testing |
| Loose `delete` reference | `hyperLOPIT` is filtered against a `delete` list with no visible definition in the notebook | Treat the filter as a no-op for fresh runs, or define an empty list |

The pickle-safety warning in `files/README.md` applies with full force here: these `.pkl` files execute code on load and are pandas-version-sensitive, so load them only from this repository with a compatible pandas version.

Sources: [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L260-L260), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1148-L1149), [07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb](/notebooks/07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb#L1296-L1296), [files/README.md](/files/README.md#L13-L13)

## Where This Fits and What to Read Next

Within the pipeline, this notebook consumes the outputs of notebooks 02 and 03 (via `files/`) and feeds compartment labels into the localization story completed by [Topology and Membrane-Leaflet Distance](15-topology-and-membrane-leaflet-distance), which resolves *within*-membrane positioning using UniProt topology annotations from the same `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` table. For the mechanical conventions shared across all 23 notebooks — pickle contracts, working-directory rules, figure naming — see [Notebook Pipeline Architecture](5-notebook-pipeline-architecture) and [Repository Layout and Notebook Map](3-repository-layout-and-notebook-map); for matching published figures to the SVG filenames generated here, consult [Figure-to-Notebook Reproducibility Map](9-figure-to-notebook-reproducibility-map). If your interest is the statistical pattern rather than the localization biology, the clustering-plus-enrichment template here is conceptually parallel to the embedding analysis in [Physicochemical Embedding and Clustering](11-physicochemical-embedding-and-clustering).


# Topology and Membrane-Leaflet Distance



This page documents `08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb`, the notebook that characterizes *where* mdSAMs live relative to membrane architecture: whether their host proteins are bitopic or polytopic, which side of the membrane (cytoplasmic, extracellular, or lumenal) the motif faces, and how many amino acids separate the motif from the nearest membrane leaflet. It produces paper panels **Fig 2B, 2C, 2D and 2F** of the manuscript, and it is the step that converts the raw mdSAM calls into a topologically annotated dataset that later analyses (motif swapping, clustering assays) build upon.
Sources: [README.md](README.md#L51), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L10-L31)

## Position in the Pipeline and Input Data

The notebook loads three shared artifacts and one external annotation file. From `dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl` it takes the high-confidence mdSAM calls (with `start_new`/`end_new` positions on the full-length sequence), deduplicated by `AAseq`. From `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` it takes transmembrane-segment coordinates (`start`/`end`) per accession, and from `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl` — the per-residue table built by notebook 02 — it takes the AlphaFold `pLDDT` arrays used to identify disordered (pLDDT < 70) residues. The fourth input is a UniProt ID-mapping TSV carrying `TOPO_DOM` annotation strings for the single-pass (bitopic) membrane proteins, fetched via an accession list of proteins with exactly one TM segment generated in-cell.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["AF2_with_ENSG.pkl<br/>(per-residue pLDDT, notebook 02)"] --> E["Topology annotation<br/>mdSAM_loc_list()"]
    B["hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl<br/>(TM segment start/end)"] --> E
    B --> I["no_TMs per protein"]
    C["dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl<br/>(mdSAM calls, dedup by AAseq)"] --> E
    D["UniProt TSV<br/>(TOPO_DOM strings, bitopics)"] --> E
    E --> F[("mdSAM_loacation.pkl<br/>location / dist / N_side")]
    F --> G["Leaflet-distance distributions<br/>Fig 2D"]
    F --> H["Juxtamembrane sliding-window<br/>chi-square obs/exp"]
    A --> H
    C --> H
    F --> J["Bitopic vs polytopic<br/>Fig 2B Fisher exact"]
    F --> K["Y/S/T phosphosite clustermaps"]
```

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L10-L31), [README.md](README.md#L40), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L77-L105)

Note the naming convention carried from the manuscript era: file names and variables use `dSAM`/`SSTM` where "SSTM" here denotes **single-segment transmembrane** proteins — the bitopic population whose topology the notebook resolves. A helper `fdr()` (Benjamini-Hochberg-style: `p × n / rank`, capped at 1) is defined early and available for multiple-testing corrections throughout the notebook.
Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L40-L48), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L77-L83)

## The Topology Annotation Engine

The core function is `mdSAM_loc_list(ind)`, which parses the UniProt `Topological domain` column of the bitopic annotation file. For a given mdSAM row it (1) extracts the orientation `side` of the first topological domain (this becomes `N_side`, e.g. `Extracellular` for type-I bitopics), (2) extracts the domain boundaries `s..e` from the `TOPO_DOM` string, and (3) assigns the motif's side label and its distance to the nearest transmembrane edge. If the mdSAM start lies *inside* the annotated domain (upstream of the TM), the distance is `TM_end − mdSAM_start`; otherwise it is `mdSAM_start − TM_end`. The result is applied across all mdSAMs whose accession exists in the annotation file, populating three new columns and persisting the annotated frame to `mdSAM_loacation.pkl`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["mdSAM start_new = m"] --> Q{"m inside domain s..e<br/>(N-terminal of TM)?"}
    Q -- "yes" --> L1["dist = TM_end − m<br/>location = first TOPO_DOM note"]
    Q -- "no" --> L2["dist = m − TM_end<br/>location = last TOPO_DOM note"]
    L1 --> O["N_side = first TOPO_DOM note<br/>(orientation of N-terminus)"]
    L2 --> O
```

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L124-L149), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L161-L176)

The annotated columns and their semantics:

| Column | Type | Meaning | Produced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | str | Membrane side of the mdSAM: `Cytoplasmic`, `Extracellular`, or `Lumenal` (organelle lumen) | `mdSAM_loc_list` via UniProt `note=` |
| `dist` | int | Amino acids from the nearest TM-segment edge to `start_new` (residue-counted, log-scale analysis downstream) | `mdSAM_loc_list` arithmetic |
| `N_side` | str | Side facing the N-terminus (`Extracellular`/`Cytoplasmic`), defining protein orientation | first `TOPO_DOM` note |
| `no_TMs` | int | Number of TM segments per protein, from `hTMs.acc.value_counts()` | later count-based cell |

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L124-L149), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L663-L675)

> [!TIP]
> The distance metric is in **residues, not nanometers** — it is the sequence separation from the TM boundary, used as a proxy for physical distance to the leaflet. Downstream 2D plots always filter `dist > 0` before plotting, so only positively-offset, side-annotated placements enter the leaflet-distance distributions.

## Distance to the Nearest Leaflet (Fig 2D)

With `location`, `dist` and the per-location counts in hand (observed: **437 cytoplasmic, 136 extracellular, 49 lumenal**), the notebook renders the leaflet-distance distributions in several iterations. The counts bar for the figure uses hardcoded histogram values replicating the observed totals, paired as an inset/side bar with the main axes. The published panel per the README map points to **cell 45** (violin plot, `mdSAM_dist_v5.svg`) and **cell 55** (stacked histogram with inset count bar, `mdSAM_dist.svg`).

| Cell (0-based) | Output SVG | Chart type | Key styling |
|---|---|---|---|
| 43 | `mdSAM_dist_v4.svg` | Boxen plot + side count bar | log-scale x, palette `#232323/#043278/#397BDE` |
| 45 | `mdSAM_dist_v5.svg` | Violin plot (inner box) + side count bar | log-scale x, ylim 1–2×10⁴ |
| 49 / 51 | `mdSAM_dist_v2.svg` | Stacked ridge: one KDE row per location | log-scale, xlim 1–10⁴, shared x-label "No. amino acids (to closest leaflet)" |
| 50 / 52 | `mdSAM_dist_v3.svg` | Single-bin stacked count bar | palette `#B96071/#679AAB/#624A64` |
| 55 | `mdSAM_dist.svg` | Stacked histogram, 15 log bins + inset axes | legend relabeled in math text |

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L663-L674), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L684-L742), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L843-L941), [README.md](README.md#L112-L113)

All variants restrict to `location ∈ {Cytoplasmic, Extracellular, Lumenal}` with `dist > 0` and place the x-axis on a log scale, spanning roughly 1 to 10⁴ residues — i.e., the analysis covers both immediately juxtamembrane motifs and motifs buried deep inside long disordered tails.
Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L685-L686), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L916-L918)

## Juxtamembrane Sliding-Window Enrichment

Beyond per-motif distance, the notebook asks a complementary question: **are mdSAM residues specifically enriched in the IDR stretch adjacent to the membrane?** For this it builds 2×2 contingency tables of residues — mdSAM vs non-mdSAM, inside vs outside a juxtamembrane window — restricted to IDR residues (pLDDT < 70) within the annotated domain, then aggregates the tables across proteins and scores them with `chi2_contingency`, recording `log2(observed/expected)` per window width.

| Residue class | In juxtamembrane window | In rest of domain IDR |
|---|---|---|
| mdSAM residues | `juxa_mdSAM` | `non_juxta_mdSAM` |
| Non-mdSAM residues | `juxa_non_mdSAM` | `non_juxta_non_mdSAM` |

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L246-L265), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L384-L420)

Two topologically mirrored scans are implemented. The **cytoplasmic scan** targets type-I bitopics (`N_side == 'Extracellular'`, cytoplasmic C-tail): version 1 takes the first `juxta_size` residues of the cytoplasmic domain; the refined version 2 uses only IDR residues and a fixed 50-residue window starting at offset `juxta_size` from the domain edge (`[sc+juxta_size, sc+50+juxta_size]`), with `juxta_size` swept `range(0, 200, 10)`. The **extracellular scan** mirrors this on the N-terminal extracellular domain of the same proteins, taking the *last* `juxta_size` residues — the window physically adjacent to the TM. The cytoplasmic result is plotted as observed-vs-expected mdSAM residues against window width; the extracellular result as the `log2(obs/exp)` enrichment curve.

| Scan | Function | Window definition | Sweep | Plot statistic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cytoplasmic v1 | `fisher_juxta_Cytoplasmic` | first `juxta_size` residues of domain | 1–200 step 25 | observed vs expected |
| Cytoplasmic v2 (final) | `fisher_juxta_Cytoplasmic_v2` | `[sc+juxta_size, sc+50+juxta_size]`, IDR-only | 0–200 step 10 | observed vs expected |
| Extracellular | `fisher_juxta_Extracellular` | last `juxta_size` residues before TM | 1–200 step 10 | `log2(obs/exp)` |

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L275-L297), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L328-L346), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L408-L420), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L441-L452), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L482-L516)

## Bitopic vs Polytopic Enrichment (Fig 2B)

The notebook counts TM segments per protein (`no_TMs` from `hTMs.acc.value_counts()`) and compares mdSAM-containing vs mdSAM-free proteins across topology classes. Crucially, it first removes **GPCRs** — identified by the Gene Ontology term `GO:0004984` (G protein-coupled receptor activity) loaded from a second UniProt ID-mapping TSV — because the 7-TM GPCR class would otherwise dominate the heptahelical bin. Binned counts (bitopic `1`, `2–6`, `7`, `>7` TM segments) are tested per bin with `fisher_exact` on the 2×2 table of mdSAM vs non-mdSAM proteins, and observed counts are compared against `expected_freq` in paired barplots.

| Bin | mdSAM proteins counted as | non-mdSAM denominator |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | distinct accs with `no_TMs == 1` | proteins outside the mdSAM set with 1 TM |
| `2–6` | distinct accs with `no_TMs ∈ [2, 6]` | same, `no_TMs ∈ [2, 6]` |
| `7` | distinct accs with `no_TMs == 7` | same, `no_TMs == 7` |
| `>7` | distinct accs with `no_TMs > 7` | same, `no_TMs > 7` |

Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L663-L666), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L971-L976), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L986-L1026), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L1084-L1099)

The intermediate cells (59–62) develop this machinery with per-TM-count variants (1–7, >7) of the same Fisher framework; the README's figure map records the final published renderings of panel 2B at **cells 70 and 73** of this notebook.
Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L1036-L1064), [README.md](README.md#L107-L108)

## Side-Specific Modification Potential (Exploratory Layer)

A self-contained sub-analysis compares cytoplasmic vs non-cytoplasmic mdSAMs for Tyr/Ser/Thr content — the phosphorylation-relevant residues. Clustered heatmaps (`sns.clustermap`, average linkage, rows = mdSAM sequences) count Y/S/T per motif: `mdSAM_YST_counts_SSTM_cyto.svg` for cytoplasmic motifs (Y+S+T) and `mdSAM_YST_counts_SSTM_non_cyto.svg` for extracellular/lumenal motifs (S+T only), each followed by a computation of the fraction of motifs carrying at least one such residue. This frames cytoplasmic mdSAMs as candidate phospho-regulated self-assembly modules — an exploratory extension of the topology theme rather than a mapped Fig 2 panel.
Sources: [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L580-L594), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L632-L655)

## Remaining Fig 2 Panels and the Exploratory Layer

Two panels of the Figure 2 family finish in this notebook per the reproducibility map: **2C** (mdSAMs at N-/C-termini vs internal loops, cells 146, 148, 168 — built directly on the `location` and `N_side` columns annotated earlier in the notebook) and **2F** (mdSAM length distribution, cell 76). Panel **2E** (mdSAMs per protein) is drawn in the companion notebook `09_mdsams_per_protein.ipynb`. Be aware that the notebook mixes published-panel cells with exploratory material: constant-sequence probes (`GSSVFLNRS`, `Q8IX19`, `Q6DN72`, `Q9ULI3`), a broken scratch cell, and superseded plot versions retained side-by-side — always consult the cell indices in the figure map when reproducing a specific panel.
Sources: [README.md](README.md#L109-L115), [08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb](notebooks/08_mdsam_topology_and_membrane_distance.ipynb#L56-L68)

> [!TIP]
> The two UniProt annotation TSVs are loaded from **absolute author-local paths** (`/Users/aelazar/notebooks_for_paper/SSTM_data/idmapping_2023_06_28.tsv` for topology and `/Users/aelazar/Downloads/idmapping_2023_11_15.tsv` for the GPCR GO terms) and are not shipped in `files/`. To rerun, regenerate them via UniProt ID mapping for the single-TM accession list produced in-cell (the SSTMs clipboard workflow), or substitute your own `Topological domain`/`Gene Ontology IDs` export with the same column schema.

## Reading Progression

This page sits between the cellular-localization and assay-analytics blocks of the Deep Dive. For the enrichment context that precedes the topology question, read [hyperLOPIT Organelle Enrichment](14-hyperlopit-organelle-enrichment); for the shared input tables consumed here (`hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl`, `dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl`, `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl`), see [Shared Data Tables Reference](8-shared-data-tables-reference); to trace any panel back to its exact notebook cell, use [Figure-to-Notebook Reproducibility Map](9-figure-to-notebook-reproducibility-map). Continuing forward, the topology characterization feeds the experimental tests of mdSAM self-assembly in [Thioflavin-T and Amytracker Screens](16-thioflavin-t-and-amytracker-screens), and the disorder-filtering prerequisite for the mdSAM set is detailed in [AlphaFold-Based Disorder Filtering](7-alphafold-based-disorder-filtering).


# Thioflavin-T and Amytracker Screens



This page documents the **in vitro self-assembly validation arm** of the mdSAM pipeline: three notebooks (`10`–`12`) that convert plate-reader fluorescence data into reproducible evidence that predicted membrane-disordered Self-Assembly Motifs (mdSAMs) form amyloid-like aggregates. Notebook 10 runs the primary 96-well Thioflavin-T (ThT) screen over synthesized mdSAM peptides, notebook 11 confirms GPCR-derived motifs with proline-mutant specificity controls, and notebook 12 provides orthogonal validation with the Amytracker 520 dye. Together they produce Figure 3A–B, Figure 4C, Figure 5B, and Supplementary Figure S3A/C/D of the manuscript. Of 44 synthesized mdSAM peptides, 36 (81%) gave ThT signal, which is the discovery paper's central in vitro result.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L84-L95), [README.md](README.md#L18-L24)

## Position in the Assay Analytics Pipeline

The dye screens sit at the transition point between computational discovery and cell-based assays. Upstream notebooks produce the mdSAM catalog and its physicochemical embedding; the screens test whether catalog members physically self-assemble; downstream notebooks ask whether that self-assembly has cellular consequences. The dependency flow below shows the three assays as a battery: ThT is the wide primary screen, the GPCR ThT panel is a targeted confirmation, and Amytracker is an orthogonal-dye replication designed to rule out ThT-specific artifacts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["mdSAM catalog<br/>dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2.pkl"] --> B["Notebook 10<br/>ThT 96-well primary screen<br/>Fig 3A-B, S3A/C"]
    B --> C["Notebook 11<br/>GPCR ThT + proline mutants<br/>Fig 4C/5B"]
    B --> D["Notebook 12<br/>Amytracker 520 replication<br/>Fig 4C, S3D"]
    C --> E["Notebook 13+<br/>TIRF puncta, flow, dSTORM"]
    D --> E
    F["Notebook 06<br/>embedding + GMM clusters"] -.->|"gmm labels<br/>+ ternary coordinates"| B
```

Notebook 10 imports cluster labels from the physicochemical embedding (`HTS/umap.pkl` refit with a 3-component Gaussian mixture) so that per-peptide ThT readouts can be stratified by charge-archetype cluster — the overlay that becomes Figure 3A.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L84-L95), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L440-L452), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L625-L660)

## Notebook 10: The 96-Well Thioflavin-T Primary Screen

**Data ingestion is a three-stage identity chain.** The screen's first problem is bookkeeping: 96 wells must be mapped to peptide sequences. Notebook 10 solves it by parsing St. Jude peptide synthesis PDF reports with `PyPDF2` (regex filters on `HC Number`, `Calculated Molecular Weight`, and `Sequence` lines yield `order_number`, `mw`, `seq` into `orederd_peptides`), reading a plate layout dictionary (`2023_11_08_Peptide_Dictionary.xlsx`) that maps each well (e.g., `A01`–`H12`) to an order number, and then joining plate-reader exports (`2023_11_08_Peptide_R*.xlsx`, one file per replicate, parsed with `header=10`) through well → order number → sequence into a tidy long-format frame with columns `well`, `nm` (wavelength), `ThT` (intensity), `rep`, and `Seq`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P["Synthesis PDFs<br/>(St. Jude reports)"] -->|PyPDF2 + regex| O["orederd_peptides<br/>order_number, mw, seq"]
    D["Peptide Dictionary xlsx<br/>well → order number"] --> W["plate_pos2seq_df"]
    R["Plate reader R*.xlsx<br/>one file per replicate"] -->|header=10| L["long-format df<br/>well, nm, ThT, rep, Seq"]
    O --> L
    W --> L
    L --> C["sequence patches +<br/>control labels"] --> S["ThT_96.pkl<br/>endpoint subset, nm == 490"]
```

Sources: [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L12-L66), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L415-L433), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L454-L530)

**Sequence patches and control wells are hardcoded after ingestion.** Three sequence strings are remapped to their intended canonical forms — the Aβ core `GYEVHHQKLVFFAED` → `YEVHHQKLVFFA`, `AGVVTTVMG` → `AGVVTTVMGS` (NGFR), and `DKVIILS` → `DKVIILSP` (TNFRSF13C) — and two special wells receive explicit labels: `H10` carries the APP benchmark peptide at double concentration (`gmm=5`, labeled `APP**`) and `C03` carries the MAPT (tau) positive control (`gmm=6`).

| Well | Role | Label | Use in analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C03` | MAPT peptide | positive control | horizontal reference line in Figure 3B (~901.3 AU) |
| `H10` | APP Aβ core, 2× | `APP**` | literature benchmark, cluster 5 |
| `H12` | background well | threshold source | hit cutoff = mean + std at 490 nm |
| DDW rows (nb 11/12) | water | negative control | log-scale floor for panels |

Sources: [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L500-L530), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L1054-L1064)

**Hit calling and visualization use 490 nm as the endpoint readout.** The full emission spectrum per well is retained in the `nm` column, but every downstream decision filters to `nm == 490`. The endpoint subset is persisted as `ThT_96.pkl` for reuse. Hit calling is deliberately simple: a peptide is scored above background when its mean intensity exceeds the `H12` mean-plus-std cutoff; the Figure 3B bar panels encode three background zones as filled bands — red below 200 AU (no signal), light gray from 200 up to the MAPT control mean, and dark gray above MAPT. Per-cluster radar charts (using a custom `radar_factory` projection) plot log-scale mean ThT with ±SEM envelopes for each GMM cluster, again with dashed reference circles at 200 and the MAPT value. The smooth convex-hull helpers (`calculate_hull`, `draw_hull` with periodic quadratic interpolation) draw the charge-archetype hulls on the embedding that become Figure 3A.

Sources: [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L1042-L1052), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L962-L1049), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L1066-L1149), [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L78-L345)

> [!TIP]
> The identity chain is indirect by design: well → order number → sequence. If you regenerate the screen with a new peptide dictionary, the three hardcoded sequence patches and the `H10`/`C03` control overrides will silently drift out of sync — re-verify them first.

## Notebook 11: GPCR mdSAMs and Proline-Mutant Specificity Controls

Notebook 11 applies the ThT assay to a targeted panel of GPCR-derived mdSAMs — the HTR7 (5HT7R) motif `VSVWVLQS`, CCR4 `VLCQYCGLLQI`, and DRD1 `LSVILDYD` — plus an extended receptor panel (DR5, DR4, IFNAR1, IFNAR2, IFNLR1, IL1R7). Its central design element is the **element taxonomy** encoded directly in row labels of the two plate-reader exports (`GPCR_ThT/Vikas_15_10_22.tsv` with 6 measurement columns, and `GPCR_ThT/Vikas_27_10_22.tsv` with 8): each label is `name_AAseq_element`, where element is `WT`, `MUT`, or `SHUFFLE`. The parser splits on `_` and stacks both batches with a `date` column (1 vs 2) so replicates across measurement days remain distinguishable.

Sources: [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L13-L17), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L19-L49), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L51-L65)

**MUT variants are single proline substitutions** that break the β-strand backbone of each motif — the assay-level analog of the HTR7 V451P mutation studied in cells later in the pipeline. The documented WT → MUT pairs:

| Protein | WT peptide | Proline mutant (MUT) |
|---|---|---|
| HTR7 (5HT7R) | `VSVWVLQS` | `VSPWVLQS` (V451P) |
| CCR4 | `VLCQYCGLLQI` | `VLCQYPGLLQI` |
| DRD1 | `LSVILDYD` | `LSVPLDYD` |
| DRD1 (2nd) | `CNLVYLIPH` | `CNLVPLIPH` |
| IFNAR1 | `KCFIIENIS` | `KCFIPENIS` |
| IFNLR1 | `QTLTFCWE` | `QTLPFCWE` |
| IFNAR2 | `DMVEVIYINRK` | `DMVEPPYINRK` |
| IL1R7 | `ITSRIFQWK` | `ITSRPFQWK` (+ `FWIRQKITS` SHUFFLE) |

Sources: [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L400-L436), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L543-L610), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L628-L662)

**Visualization is strip-plus-point panels on a log fluorescence axis**, black for WT and red for MUT, with a thin vertical reference line at the mean ThT of the water (`DDW`) wells. The final Figure 5B panel (`GPCR_paper.svg`) is a 4-row figure — 5HT7R, CCR4, DRD1, H₂O — with superscripted residue-position labels (⁴⁴⁹, ³²⁷, ³⁸⁵, ⁴²⁰) anchoring each motif in its parent protein sequence; `GCPR_ThT.svg` is the wider Fig 4C/5B layout, and the `Thiru_good`/`Thiru_bad` panels split the extended receptor panel by whether the proline mutant abolishes signal. A `seq2name_df` lookup maps each sequence back to its gene name for the twin-axis annotation. Per the figure map, cells 16–17 produce the HTR7 WT vs V451P comparison (Fig 4C/5B) and cell 32 the GPCR ThT spectra (Fig 5B).

Sources: [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L400-L436), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L700-L745), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L748-L758), [README.md](README.md#L160-L170)

## Notebook 12: Amytracker 520 Orthogonal Validation

Notebook 12 is the smallest of the three and follows a strict replication logic: it re-tests the GPCR motif panel with a chemically different amyloid dye. Data comes from a single Excel export (`CD/20260115_Amytracker520.xlsx`, `header=9`) whose instrument layout places the fluorescence channel in a raw column named `' Raw Data  (470-15/513-20)'`; rows are filtered to `Concentration (uM) == 100` and the six assayed peptides (`APP`, `DRD1`, `5HTR7`, `CCR4`, `IFNAR2`, `IFNAR1`). The figure is a hollow-bar grouped plot with `hue='Element'` separating `WT` from `MUT`, and a dashed horizontal line at the median of the `Control` peptide wells. Statistical support is a one-sided `stats.ttest_ind(..., alternative='greater')` per peptide testing WT > MUT, run for IFNAR2, 5HTR7, DRD1, and CCR4. Output: `Amytracker_100uM.svg` (Fig 4C; S3D).

Sources: [notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb](notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb#L13-L17), [notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb](notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb#L22-L32), [notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb](notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb#L34-L58)

> [!TIP]
> The Amytracker channel column name contains a leading space and double internal spaces (`' Raw Data  (470-15/513-20)'`) exactly as exported by the reader software — any `df[column]` access must reproduce that string verbatim, so copy it rather than retyping it.

## Cross-Assay Comparison

The three notebooks form one evidentiary argument with complementary designs. ThT in notebook 10 maximizes breadth (44 peptides, full spectra, cluster stratification); ThT in notebook 11 maximizes specificity (paired WT/MUT/SHUFFLE on targeted motifs); Amytracker in notebook 12 maximizes robustness (orthogonal dye chemistry on the key GPCR panel).

| Dimension | Notebook 10 (ThT primary) | Notebook 11 (GPCR ThT) | Notebook 12 (Amytracker) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input | Synthesis PDFs + dictionary + `R*.xlsx` (3 reps) | Two TSV reader exports (`date` 1–2) | One Excel export, `header=9` |
| Format | 96-well plate, emission spectra | Plate rows, 6–8 reads per peptide | 100 µM endpoint reads |
| Readout | ThT @ 490 nm (endpoint of `nm` scan) | ThT @ 490 nm, log axis | Amytracker 520 channel (470/513) |
| Specificity controls | APP** and MAPT references, background bands | MUT (proline) + SHUFFLE per motif | MUT (proline) per motif |
| Statistics | H12 mean+std cutoff; SEM envelopes | Descriptive strip/point panels | One-sided t-tests (WT > MUT) |
| Persistence | `ThT_96.pkl` | — (SVG figures only) | — (SVG figure only) |
| Paper panels | Fig 3A–B; S3A, S3C | Fig 4C, 5B; S3C | Fig 4C; S3D |

Sources: [notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb](notebooks/10_tht_peptide_screen_96well.ipynb#L1042-L1052), [notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb](notebooks/11_tht_gpcr_peptides_proline_mutants.ipynb#L13-L49), [notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb](notebooks/12_amytracker_peptides.ipynb#L22-L58), [README.md](README.md#L84-L95)

**Reproducibility caveats.** All three notebooks contain absolute local paths (macOS user directories under `/Users/aelazar/...`) for the raw instrument files and intermediate pickles, and the distributed notebooks ship with outputs cleared — rerunning them requires placing the raw reader exports, the peptide dictionary, and the embedding pickles at the referenced locations, or editing the path constants. The key reusable intermediate is `ThT_96.pkl`; notebook 11 and 12 operate entirely in-memory from raw files. The manuscript's figure map (`FIGURE_MAP.csv`) pins each panel to notebook and 0-based cell index: Figure 3A from cells 25–26 and Figure 3B from cells 54/73 of notebook 10, cells 16/17 of notebook 11, and cell 3 of notebook 12.
